messages:
Maya: Heads-up — I'm seeing that the pressed state for our 'primary-ghost' and 'icon-flat' buttons is barely visible at 16/20px on the dashboard row actions. On the compact table the click feels unregistered. Mock: https://img.redwood/design/press-state-issue.png
Kevin: I noticed that too. On slow devices the scale animation (our only affordance) is tiny; reduced-motion users get zero feedback. Current CSS we ship:
```css
.button { transition: transform 120ms ease; }
.button:active { transform: scale(0.98); }
```
Sophie: Suggestion — add a subtle inset shadow + a very slight dark overlay on press. Keeps things instant when motion is off. E.g. box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.12) + background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0.06).
Darren: Careful: inset shadow can be read as a focus ring by users. We should differentiate focus (outline) vs press (inset + overlay). Focus must remain visible for keyboard users.
A11yBot: Note: any color overlay needs to be perceivable. Aim for a minimum 3:1 perceptual change against the default background so low-vision users notice the state change. Also ensure reduced-motion users still get a non-motion visual change.
FrontendInfra: I can prototype a CSS variant that falls back for prefers-reduced-motion. Something like:
```css
.button--pressed { box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.12); background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0.06); }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .button { transform: none; } }
```
Kevin: +1. Also think we should make the pressed state instant (no easing) and then animate release. Instant-on, quick-off works better for perceived responsiveness: 0-50ms show, 120ms revert.
Maya: Good call. Another micro UX note — 'Retry' and 'Copy' actions in rows: pressing currently triggers a toast which appears after the spinner. Users expect immediate visual confirmation. If we add the inset overlay instantly and a subtle aria-live toast "Action started", that'll help.
Sophie: From tokens perspective, maybe add a small token for press overlay alpha rather than hardcoding (e.g., color.press.overlay = rgba(var(--ink), 0.06)). But let's avoid new tokens unless we foresee widespread reuse.
Darren: I'll make sure QA checks include verifying that press != focus. Also list the behavior matrix: mouse press, keyboard enter/space, touch tap, reduced-motion.
FrontendInfra: Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/2345 — implements the pressed variant, prefers-reduced-motion fallback, and demo page for 16/20px buttons. Tested on iOS Safari and Android Chrome; looks consistent.
Maya: I'll update the Figma with both motion and no-motion states and include the overlay token suggestion. We'll run a small canary with product for a week (A/B: current vs inset overlay).
A11yBot: Quick checklist: 1) Press visual change perceivable without motion, 2) Focus ring unchanged for keyboard, 3) Screen reader sees aria-live feedback for async ops.
Kevin: One last nudge — animations should not shift layout or change hit targets. Keep press purely visual.
Maya: Thanks team. I'll drop final specs in the design kit and add a short note to the release brief. :thumbsup:
